label: Глава
description: A 10-sentence usage card for глава (chapter; head).

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Глава' is the feminine nominative subject of 'была'. 'Первая' agrees, and 'интересной' is the instrumental predicate adjective after 'была'.
Strategic focus: Accusative object. 'Главу' is the feminine accusative direct object of 'прочитал'. 'Последнюю' agrees in the feminine accusative, and 'вчера' adds the time.
Strategic focus: Genitive of relation. 'Главы' is the feminine genitive after 'конец', expressing the end of the chapter. The phrase 'без ответа' adds the genitive of absence.
Strategic focus: Dative after к. 'Главе' is the feminine dative governed by 'к', the point returned to. 'Первой' agrees in the feminine dative.
Strategic focus: Instrumental after стать. 'Главой' is the feminine instrumental required by 'стал', the role he became, here in the sense of head. 'Компании' is the genitive showing what he heads.
Strategic focus: Prepositional case. 'О главе' uses the prepositional form after 'о' to mean discussing the chapter. 'Следующей' agrees in the feminine prepositional.
Strategic focus: Nominative plural subject. 'Главы' is the nominative plural subject of the implicit linking clause. 'Первые' agrees and 'книги' is the genitive showing whose chapters.
Strategic focus: Genitive plural after quantity. 'Глав' is the genitive plural required by 'несколько', with the fleeting vowel dropping. 'Романа' is the genitive naming whose chapters.
Strategic focus: Genitive plural after numeral. 'Глав' is the genitive plural required after the numeral 'двадцать'. The place phrase 'в книге' frames where they are.
Strategic focus: Nominative plural subject. 'Главы' is the nominative plural subject of 'встретились', here in the sense of heads of state. 'Государств' is the genitive plural specifying which heads.
